text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu rejected Hussein's plea to postspone construction at Har Homa; considering gesture to Arafat.
- Defence establishment concerned air force's former chief acquisitions officer Rami Dotan will leak to the U.S. that Israel was involved in bribery affair.
- Interior Ministry confiscating hundreds of identification cards from Palestinians in East Jerusalem.
JERUSALEM POST
- Gaza airport now open for Arafat.
- Erekat denies secret talks.
- Hussein visit shows strength of peace with Jordan.
- Strauss family debating possible Elite takeover.
- Heineken purchases 51 percent of Tempo.
- Long-term savings 19 percent.
- Ares-Serono completes InterPharm takeover.
MAARIV
- Talks underway to prepare Netanyahu-Arafat summit.
- King Hussein caressed, consoled.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Crisis with Palestinians eased; negotiations resume today.
- Arafat gave Hamas green light for guerrilla attacks.
- More criticism over decision for early release of Rami Dotan.
GLOBES
- Strass received five offers to join Elite group.
